messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `test_changeDefault_Locale_DateInstance` in `FastDateFormatTest` fails because the behavior of `FastDateFormat.getDateInstance()` does not correctly handle changes to the default Locale during runtime. The test sets the default Locale to US, then creates a `FastDateFormat` instance with a specific Locale (Germany) and one with the default Locale. It then changes the default Locale to Germany and creates another instance with the default Locale. The expected behavior is that the Locale for each instance reflects either the explicitly given Locale or the default Locale at the time of construction.

From the code of `FastDateFormat.getDateInstance(int style, TimeZone timeZone, Locale locale)`, we see that the method uses a cache (a HashMap) keyed by style, optional timezone, and optional locale. If `locale` is `null`, it is not used in the key; instead, the default Locale at the time of creation (`Locale.getDefault()`) is used to create the `FastDateFormat`. This means that if the default Locale changes after the fact, the cached entry keyed without a locale will point to an instance created with an old default Locale, causing subsequent calls with `locale=null` (i.e., relying on default) to return the old cached instance, not a new one respecting the new default.

In the test, the first call `getDateInstance(FULL, Locale.GERMANY)` creates a cached entry keyed with the Locale.GERMANY. The second call `getDateInstance(FULL)` is equivalent to `getDateInstance(FULL, null)` and caches an instance keyed without any locale but created with the then default Locale (US). Changing the default Locale to Germany and calling `getDateInstance(FULL)` again looks up the cache with the same key (no locale), returning the previously cached format created with Locale.US, but the test expects the locale to match the new default Locale (Germany). Hence, `format3.getLocale()` returns `Locale.US` instead of `Locale.GERMANY`.

This confirms the problem described in the bug report: "FastDateFormat getDateInstance() and getDateTimeInstance() assume Locale.getDefault() won't change". The key creation omits the locale if null, thus caching instances that are tied to the default Locale at construction time, but not refreshing or invalidating them when the default Locale changes, causing inconsistency.

Other methods like `getDateTimeInstance` have a similar caching strategy with the same flaw.

Therefore, the root cause is the caching mechanism's treating a null locale as "no locale" key but caching instances bound to the default Locale at creation time, making it inconsistent if the default Locale changes later.

This was evidenced by:
- The test setting and changing default locales.
- The bug report describing the assumption of default Locale never changing.
- The source code snippet showing the cache keys and construction logic.
- The `getLocale()` method returning the bound Locale which disagrees with expectations after default Locale change.

Fixing this would require changing how the cache key is built or forcing a refresh when the default Locale changes, or never caching entries with null locale as a single key, to avoid stale Locale binding.

Suggested fix focus is on the cache key building and instance retrieval in `getDateInstance` and `getDateTimeInstance`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

FastDateFormat.getDateInstance(int, java.util.TimeZone, java.util.Locale)
FastDateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(int, int, java.util.TimeZone, java.util.Locale)
